title: Invoke endpoints (issue detection, GenAI evaluate, scorer): caller-supplied trace_ids must belong to the authorized experiment before any run or job is created
answers: Why can a user run issue detection on traces from an experiment they cannot read?
Where is the check that trace ids belong to the experiment being invoked on issues/invoke handled?
Adding a new field or provider to the GenAI evaluate invoke request: where do trace ids get validated?
Why does a rejected invoke request create no evaluation run?
body:
Path: mlflow/server/handlers.py:_invoke_issue_detection_handler, _invoke_genai_evaluate_handler and _invoke_scorer_handler handle the POST /ajax-api/3.0/mlflow/issues/invoke, genai/evaluate/invoke and scorer/invoke requests (trace_ids plus experiment_id, credentials, scorers); all three pass trace_ids through mlflow/server/handlers.py:_validate_trace_ids_in_experiment.
Rule: The route validators (validate_can_update_experiment) only check the caller's permission on the request's experiment_id and never look at trace_ids. Any new invoke-style handler that accepts trace_ids must call _validate_trace_ids_in_experiment(store, trace_ids, experiment_id) before fetching credentials, resolving scorers, creating a run or submitting a job, so a rejected request leaves no run and no job.
Symptom: A user who could update their own experiment supplied trace ids from another experiment; the job analyzed those traces and wrote the results into the caller's run (broken object authorization, GHSA-v7w2-x9m4-3743).
Constraints: The helper raises a generic PERMISSION_DENIED (403, message 'Not all requested traces could be accessed.') only when an existing trace resolves to a different experiment. Missing traces are not rejected here; they fail later in the job. The check lives in the handler rather than the auth validators so it also protects deployments that mount the handlers without the basic-auth app.
applies: Any server handler that takes caller-supplied trace_ids alongside an experiment_id to start a job or write assessments/runs.
says: A user who can update one experiment can run issue detection on traces from another experiment
Issue detection job writes results into my run using trace IDs from a different experiment
Trace IDs from another experiment are accepted by GenAI evaluate and scorer invoke requests
Rejected evaluation or issue detection request should not create a run or job
Trace IDs must belong to the experiment being used before any evaluation or issue job starts
search: Invoke endpoints for issue detection, GenAI evaluate and scorer: caller-supplied trace IDs must belong to the authorized experiment via a shared validation helper, run before credentials, scorer resolution, run creation or job submission. Permission check on experiment_id alone is insufficient; a rejected request creates no run or job. Missing traces are not rejected here.
